findings.title: msg.value Reuse Across MultiCommand execute() Loop
findings.description: execute() iterates over commands with msg.value unchanged. WRAP_ETH can be called multiple times consuming residual ETH held in VaultRouter. The contract's receive() accepts all ETH without sender validation, allowing an attacker to steal any ETH left in the router by repeatedly issuing WRAP_ETH commands in a single multicall.

findings.title: Missing Access Control on StrategySwapAnd deploy()/undeploy()
findings.description: deploy() and undeploy() lack the onlyOwner modifier. Any caller can invoke undeploy() and receive funds via safeTransfer(msg.sender, ...). All SwapAnd strategy variants are affected, enabling complete drain of strategy TVL by any external actor.

findings.title: Default Zero Slippage Protection in Leverage Strategies
findings.description: _maxSlippage initializes to 0 in StrategyLeverageSettings, causing all swaps to execute with amountOutMinimum = 0. MEV searchers can extract 10–30% value from every deploy, undeploy, and harvest operation via sandwich attacks with no lower bound on output.

findings.title: Oracle Staleness Bypass in totalAssets() via maxAge=0
findings.description: totalAssets() calls the oracle with maxAge: 0, which disables all staleness checks. During Chainlink delays or outages, the stale price is silently accepted, enabling arbitrage between the stale on-chain price and the real market price at the expense of vault depositors.

findings.title: StrategySupplyERC4626 Reports Shares as Assets
findings.description: _getBalance() returns _vault.balanceOf() (the share balance) instead of convertToAssets(). For any ERC-4626 vault with accrued yield, this causes totalAssets() to be systematically underreported, mispricing shares for all depositors and breaking downstream accounting.

findings.title: ExRateOracle Uses MAX Instead of MIN for lastUpdate
findings.description: The combined lastUpdate timestamp uses the MAX of component timestamps, masking stale ratio data when only the base price is fresh. getSafeLatestPrice() performs no staleness check on the combined result. Additionally, CustomExRateOracle sets ratio.lastUpdate = 0, permanently bypassing staleness validation.

findings.title: PULL_TOKEN_FROM Allows Arbitrary from Address
findings.description: PULL_TOKEN_FROM and PUSH_TOKEN_FROM accept a fully caller-controlled from address. Any outstanding approval a user has given to VaultRouter can be drained by any other caller by passing the victim's address as the from parameter, enabling theft of all tokens approved to the router.

findings.title: No Reentrancy Guard on VaultRouter.execute()
findings.description: execute() lacks the nonReentrant modifier. External calls to vaults and DEX routers within the command loop can re-enter the router, corrupting the shared callStack state mid-execution and enabling manipulation of intermediate results across commands.

findings.title: addStrategy() Missing Asset Check and Approval
findings.description: addStrategy() does not validate that the new strategy's underlying asset matches the vault's asset, nor does it issue a safeApprove to the strategy. New strategies therefore cannot receive token deployments, causing a DoS on deployment. An asset mismatch can also inflate totalAssets with phantom value.

findings.title: First Depositor / Donation Attack
findings.description: An attacker can deposit a minimal amount to become the first shareholder, then donate tokens directly to the vault to inflate the share price. Subsequent depositors receive 0 shares due to integer truncation with no shares > 0 guard in _depositInternal, enabling complete theft of subsequent deposits.

findings.title: CurveFi EXACT_OUTPUT Overspend
findings.description: The EXACT_OUTPUT swap path correctly calculates requiredIn as the minimum input needed, but then passes params.amountIn (the full maximum) to the actual swap call. Excess tokens beyond requiredIn are consumed from the strategy and permanently stuck in the contract rather than being returned.

findings.title: DEX Swap Deadline Uses block.timestamp
findings.description: UniV2Library and AerodromeLibrary pass block.timestamp as the swap deadline. Since block.timestamp always equals the current block, this provides no MEV protection: validators and searchers can hold and replay the transaction at any future block with no deadline enforcement.

findings.title: StrategySupplyBase.undeploy() Accounting Mismatch
findings.description: _deployedAmount is not updated after undeploy, leaving the tracked balance stale. The function also returns the requested amount rather than the actual withdrawalValue received from the underlying protocol, causing phantom loss reports during harvest and misleading downstream accounting.

findings.title: _pendingAmount Not Cleared After undeploy
findings.description: _pendingAmount is intentionally not cleared after undeploy 'to save gas', leaving stale state that persists across subsequent operations. This creates a latent vulnerability where residual pending amounts can interfere with future leverage accounting.

findings.title: Governor Can Replace Oracle Without Timelock
findings.description: setDebtOracle() allows the governor to instantly replace the debt oracle with no timelock, delay, or validation of the new oracle's return values. An attacker who compromises the governor key (or a malicious governor) can immediately substitute a manipulated oracle and drain the protocol.

findings.title: Raw .approve()/.transfer() Fail With Non-Standard Tokens
findings.description: Multiple contracts use raw IERC20.approve() and IERC20.transfer() which revert for tokens like USDT that return no boolean value. VaultBase's withdrawal path uses raw .transfer() instead of SafeERC20.safeTransfer(), bricking strategies and blocking withdrawals for non-standard ERC-20 assets.

findings.title: PULL_TOKEN Dispatch Bug
findings.description: The PULL_TOKEN handler compares the full 256-bit action value instead of actionToExecute, causing the callStack-mapped PULL_TOKEN path to never match. Any command that routes PULL_TOKEN through a callStack mapping silently falls through without executing, breaking intended multicall flows.

findings.title: _deallocateAssets() Truncation Shortfall
findings.description: The per-strategy fraction calculation in _deallocateAssets() uses integer truncation, systematically losing the remainder when dividing the total withdrawal amount across multiple strategies. This results in the protocol consistently underpaying users on multi-strategy withdrawals.

findings.title: _harvestAndMintFees Pre-Harvest Denominator
findings.description: The performance fee share calculation uses the pre-harvest totalAssets as the denominator when minting fee shares. This causes systematic over-dilution of existing shareholders because the denominator should reflect the post-harvest value that includes the newly accrued yield.

findings.title: uint16 Truncation in VaultRouter Dispatch
findings.description: VaultRouter casts 32-bit callStack mapping fields to uint16 during dispatch, silently discarding the upper 16 bits. This corrupts routing for callStack slots 3 and 4 (values above 0xFFFF), causing commands that reference those slots to read from the wrong position.

findings.title: Missing Zero-Shares Check After Deploy Slippage
findings.description: After the toBase() calculation in _depositInternal, there is no check that shares > 0. If slippage or rounding during an active leverage deploy causes the computed share count to truncate to zero, the depositor permanently loses their assets while receiving nothing in return.

findings.title: ChainLink Missing answeredInRound Check
findings.description: The standard Chainlink safety check comparing answeredInRound >= roundId is not performed in ChainLinkOracle. While partially mitigated by the maxAge staleness check, incomplete round validation can allow use of prices from incomplete or invalid rounds under specific oracle conditions.

findings.title: StrategySupplyBase.harvest() No Access Control
findings.description: harvest() has no access control modifier, allowing any external caller to trigger it at will. An adversary can manipulate _deployedAmount tracking by forcing harvests at unfavorable times, potentially distorting yield accounting and fee calculations.

findings.title: Withdrawal Rounding Favors User in Violation of ERC-4626
findings.description: convertToShares uses roundUp=false for withdrawals, rounding in favor of the withdrawing user rather than the vault. ERC-4626 requires withdrawal share conversion to round up to protect remaining depositors. This violates the spec and can cause small but systematic losses to the vault over many withdrawals.

findings.title: Unsafe .transfer() in PythOracle ETH Refund
findings.description: getLatestPrice() refunds excess ETH to the caller using .transfer(), which forwards only 2300 gas. Smart contract callers with non-trivial receive() or fallback() functions will fail to receive the refund, causing the entire oracle call to revert and making the oracle inaccessible to those callers.

findings.title: Inconsistent Zero-Address Validation in UseIERC4626
findings.description: withdrawVault() is missing the vault zero-address check that is present in depositVault(), mintVault(), and redeemVault(). This inconsistency could allow a withdrawal call with a zero vault address to proceed, potentially causing unexpected reverts or undefined behavior in downstream calls.
